topPRs.title: op-acceptance-tests: cover proofs re-execution across a sequencer reorg
topPRs.author: einar-oplabs
topPRs.body:
## Why

The proofs-history ExEx handles a reth reorg notification by unwinding its store to the fork point and indexing the replacement blocks from reth's trie data; a follower on the re-execution path (`--proofs-history.verification-interval=1`) then executes every block that follows against the unwound state, including calls into code that only a replacement block created. The only coverage was an ExEx unit test with a hand-built replacement block; the real notification sequence of a sequencer reorg, with a fork point in reth's memory or below its persisted tip, had never been run against the proof oracle. #23046 changes what happens when a replaced block fails re-execution, so this is the acceptance coverage for it.

## What

**`op-acceptance-tests/tests/proofs_history_reorg`** (sequencer without proofs history as the `eth_getProof` reference and the node the test sequencer drives, follower re-executing every block, 1s L2 blocks, both op-reths with `--engine.persistence-threshold` and `--engine.memory-block-buffer-target=5` passed explicitly):

- `TestProofsHistoryFollowerMatchesTheReplacementChainAfterASequencerReorg`: the batcher is stopped up front so the replaced blocks never reach L1; four EOAs are funded, traffic runs past the setup and op-node's sequencer stops, which makes its head the fork point; an in-memory cell then pads the chain with empty test-sequencer blocks until the replaced blocks will leave the fork point in reth's memory by the persistence model, so the fork point does not depend on where the stop landed. The test sequencer then builds the `depth` blocks the reorg will replace on top of it, no faster than wall-clock (op-node rejects a gossiped payload more than 5s ahead), and the follower imports them by gossip and re-executes them; the test waits until its proofs store has flushed the last of them. The test sequencer then builds one conflicting block on the fork point, the batcher restarts and op-node resumes sequencing on top of it. The follower must adopt the replacement chain (`ReorgExact` on the first replaced height), survive (no `panicked` line), catch up, serve the replacement block with its transactions, and after ten more blocks of traffic `VerifyHistoricalProofsMatch` sweeps every block from the fork point to the last traffic block for the four EOAs and, in the deployed-contract workload, the recorder's two slots; that workload also requires the recorder's slot 0 on the follower to hold a block number above the fork point. Finally the follower's op-reth log must show the ExEx reorg notification and the proofs engine unwinding stored blocks, and must show reth's "on-disk reorg detected" line exactly in the on-disk cells.
- Workloads: `deployed_contract` (the first replaced block deploys the `NUMBER`/`TIMESTAMP` recorder and the replaced blocks after it call it; the replacement block carries the same deployment transaction, so the contract exists at the same address, plus a call into it; the traffic after the reorg keeps calling it) and `plain_transfers`.
- Depths per threshold: 2 (fork point among the blocks reth never persisted), 6 (deeper than the memory block buffer target, fork point still in memory; at threshold 7 reth holds 5 to 7 blocks, so up to two padding blocks are needed), and 12 at threshold 7 / 55 at threshold 50 (below reth's persisted tip: on-disk reorg). `blocksInRethMemory` models reth's persistence schedule and `matrix_test.go` pins it; the assertion on reth's own "on-disk reorg detected" line, present in exactly the on-disk cells, catches a wrong model instead of silently testing the other path. Note the issue's "threshold + 5" bound for the on-disk depth is conservative: reth holds at most `threshold` blocks (it persists once the head is more than the threshold above the persisted tip, down to the head minus the buffer target).

Matrix, as table-driven subtests: threshold {7, 50} x masking {0, 30} x workload {deployed_contract, plain_transfers} x depth {in memory shallow, in memory deep, on disk}. The masking cells skip naming ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#457. Under `DEVSTACK_L2CL_KIND=kona-node` every cell skips: the test sequencer commits and publishes blocks through op-node's `opstack_commitBlockV1`/`opstack_publishBlockV1` RPCs, which kona-node does not serve.

**`op-devstack`** seams:

- Log recorder: `logpipe.LogRecord` (entries whose message, or raw text for a line that is not structured JSON such as a panic hook's output, contains a substring) and `logpipe.LogRecords` (fan-out), `stack.LogRecorder`, `sysgo.OpReth.RecordLogLines(substring)` recording every stdout and stderr line at every level across restarts, forwarded by the preset `l2ELFrontend`, and `dsl.L2ELNode.RecordLogLines(substring)`, which fails for a node whose log the devstack does not expose. `logpipe.StructuredRustLogEntry.UnparsedLine()` exposes the raw text of an unstructured line.
- `dsl.EOA.PlanBlockRecorderDeployment()`: the recorder deployment as a planned transaction, so a test can keep its signed bytes; `DeployBlockRecorder` uses it.
- `dsl.TestSequencer.SequenceBlockWithTxs` closes out the job with `Next` after a successful publish (every step is already done, so `Next` only resets), which lets consecutive blocks be sequenced on one chain; before, the second `New` failed with `block already sealed`. No existing caller sequenced two blocks on the same chain. A block that was not published still leaves the job sealed, as before, now with a warning.
- `dsl.TestSequencer.SequenceBlockWithTxsWhenDue(t, network, parent, rawTxs)`: builds the block no earlier than its timestamp (fixed by its height) so op-node's gossip validation accepts it on publish and on receipt. The wait is a wall-clock wait inside the DSL, since the chain stands still while the test sequencer drives it.

Deleted `rust/op-reth/tests/proofs/reorg/reorg_test.go`: dormant (CI runs `proofs/core` only), it used sleeps and tested the index path; its reorg coverage is superseded here. Unit tests: `TestLogRecordKeepsMatchingEntriesInOrder`, `TestLogRecordMatchesTheRawTextOfUnstructuredLines`, `TestLogRecordEntriesIsACopy`, `TestLogRecordsFanOutFromRegistration`, `TestBlocksInRethMemory`, `TestInMemoryDepthsFitRethMemoryWithinOnePersistenceCycle`, `TestOnDiskDepthsExceedRethMemory`.

## Findings

- How a CL-synced follower adopts an unsafe reorg: op-node drops every gossiped block that does not extend its unsafe chain (`skipping unsafe payload, since it is older than unsafe head` / `does not build onto the existing unsafe chain`), so the replacement blocks below its head never get in through gossip. Once a gossiped block above its head arrives, `checkForGapInUnsafeQueue` hands it to reth with `engine_newPayload`; reth fetches the missing replacement blocks from its EL peer (`Block added to fork chain`) and makes the forkchoice target canonical once they connect. The follower switched 2s after op-node resumed in the in-memory cells and 4s in the on-disk ones; L1 derivation was not involved. The batcher still has to be off while the replaced blocks are built, or they become safe and the fork is impossible.
- The bump's `Block left reth's chain during proofs execution` line (and develop's `Parent state not available in reth; skipping execute_block` skip) only fires when the ExEx is mid-execution of a block of the old chain at the instant reth reorgs. With a real reorg the ExEx has long finished the old chain by then (it executes a block in about a millisecond), so neither line appeared in any cell (`parent_state_missing_skips=0 left_chain_handoffs=0`), and neither can be asserted deterministically without a seam that delays ExEx execution. The test records both counts and logs them; the issue's expectation that a deeper reorg makes the line appear does not hold.
- The reorg notification carries the whole replacement chain in one go: `reorg_depth=4 common_ancestor=20` for a depth-2 reorg, since reth connects the fetched blocks and the block that followed before it switches.
- On develop every cell matches the oracle, including the on-disk reorgs at both thresholds (reth rebuilds the replaced persisted blocks with overlay-computed trie updates for the notification, and the ExEx's fork-block check holds).

## Local verification

Debug op-reth built from this branch, `DEVSTACK_ORCHESTRATOR=sysgo RUST_BINARY_PATH_OP_RETH=<debug op-reth> go test -count=1 -timeout 60m -parallel 2 -v -run TestProofsHistoryFollowerMatchesTheReplacementChainAfterASequencerReorg ./op-acceptance-tests/tests/proofs_history_reorg/`:

```
--- PASS: TestProofsHistoryFollowerMatchesTheReplacementChainAfterASequencerReorg
    threshold_7-masking_0-deployed_contract-depth_2_in_memory    (57.10s)  fork point 20, sweep 20..46, 6 accounts
    threshold_7-masking_0-plain_transfers-depth_2_in_memory      (55.88s)  fork point 19, sweep 19..45
    threshold_7-masking_0-deployed_contract-depth_6_in_memory    (48.69s)  fork point 19, sweep 19..41
    threshold_7-masking_0-plain_transfers-depth_6_in_memory      (48.91s)  fork point 19, sweep 19..41
    threshold_7-masking_0-deployed_contract-depth_12_on_disk     (61.13s)  fork point 19, sweep 19..53, on-disk reorg logged
    threshold_7-masking_0-plain_transfers-depth_12_on_disk       (65.72s)  fork point 20, sweep 20..56, on-disk reorg logged
    threshold_50-masking_0-deployed_contract-depth_2_in_memory   (57.10s)  fork point 20, sweep 20..46
    threshold_50-masking_0-plain_transfers-depth_2_in_memory     (56.94s)  fork point 20, sweep 20..46
    threshold_50-masking_0-deployed_contract-depth_6_in_memory   (48.77s)  fork point 19, sweep 19..41
    threshold_50-masking_0-plain_transfers-depth_6_in_memory     (48.97s)  fork point 19, sweep 19..41
    threshold_50-masking_0-deployed_contract-depth_55_on_disk   (108.42s)  fork point 19, sweep 19..98, on-disk reorg logged
    threshold_50-masking_0-plain_transfers-depth_55_on_disk     (108.06s)  fork point 19, sweep 19..98, on-disk reorg logged
    12 masking_30 cells skipped (protocol-team#457)
ok      op-acceptance-tests/tests/proofs_history_reorg  386.880s
```

Every cell logged `reorg_notified=1 reorg_handled=1`, the on-disk cells `on_disk_reorg=1` and the others `0`; no cell needed padding blocks in this run (the depth-6 cells at threshold 7 stopped on heights with seven blocks in memory). The same matrix passed once more before the review changes (401.965s).

```
go vet ./op-devstack/... ./op-acceptance-tests/tests/proofs_history_reorg/ ./op-service/logpipe/      # ok
go test -count=1 ./op-service/logpipe/ ./op-acceptance-tests/tests/proofs_history_reorg/ -run 'TestLogRecord|TestBlocksInRethMemory|TestInMemoryDepths|TestOnDiskDepths'   # ok
./linter/bin/op-golangci-lint run ./op-devstack/... ./op-service/logpipe/... ./op-acceptance-tests/tests/proofs_history_reorg/...   # ok
go test -count=1 ./op-devstack/sysgo/ -run 'TestProofsHistoryNodeArgs|TestOpRethWith|TestSubProcess|TestL2CLVerifierSyncMode'   # ok
```

CI budget: the twelve cells sum to about 13 minutes back to back, so the package stays under 20 minutes with `-parallel 1`.

Not run: the kona-node variant (every cell skips under it, see above).

## Skipped cells

- All `masking_30` cells: ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#457.
- Every cell under `DEVSTACK_L2CL_KIND=kona-node`: the test sequencer's commit/publish RPCs are op-node only.

Stacked on #23421 and #23418.

Closes #23383

topPRs.title: op-reth: model-based test of the proofs engine state machine
topPRs.author: einar-oplabs
topPRs.body:
A randomized, model-based test of the proofs engine (`rust/op-reth/crates/trie/src/engine`): random interleavings of commits, reorgs, reverts, sync targets, flushes, failed saves, stale notifications and crashes, driven over reth's persistence model, with the store and the engine held to a reference model after every step. The engine's bugs are interleaving bugs (ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#464, #477, #478), and the deterministic cases of #23441 and #23449 only cover the interleavings someone thought of.

## What the test does

New integration target `rust/op-reth/crates/trie/tests/engine_model.rs` (its own target so that it and the live target do not share a time budget):

- **Reference model** (`tests/engine_model/model.rs`): the canonical chain as the consensus layer holds it (hash, parent, state root per block), the proof window, a lower bound on what the store has persisted, the fork points whose hash the engine holds for certain, and the engine's possible states as a small set of `(tip, sync target)` candidates. Saves and the sync loop run in the background, so the model predicts a set of outcomes per step and the harness narrows it with the tip it observes once the engine settles. It knows nothing of the engine's internals.
- **Simulated reth**: the existing `SimulatedReth` from `tests/live/simulated_reth.rs` (a real `BlockchainProvider` driven by reth's threshold rule), extended with `revert_to`, `crash_and_restart` (loses everything above reth's persisted tip and reopens from the database) and a `persisted` accessor. Faults: a store wrapper whose next write transaction fails (`tests/engine_model/faults.rs`, for a failed save), and a block reported as replaced through a stale `ChainCommitted` delivered after reth reorged it away (the execute path then finds no parent state).
- **Actions** (`tests/engine_model/actions.rs`), chosen per step with proptest: `Commit{n}`, `Reorg{depth, length}`, `Revert{depth}`, `SyncTo{n}` (reth commits `n` blocks the engine only learns of through a sync target), `Flush`, `FailNextSave`, `StaleCommit{depth, length}`, `BogusReorg` (a one-block reorg on a parent no block has, at a fork point the engine knows), and `Crash(Same)` (drop the engine without flushing, reopen the store, spawn a fresh engine, `sync_to(best)`, then reth rebuilds the lost blocks from the same chain and the harness delivers them as live notifications, with no WAL replay). `Crash(Different)` exists but only the tracked-bug run enables it.
- **Invariants after every step** (`tests/engine_model/invariants.rs`): the engine settles on a tip the model predicts within 30 s; the store's earliest and latest blocks are on the canonical chain; the latest is at or below the engine's tip and at or above what the store had persisted; the window holds at most its configured size; the stored state at the window's ends and at the last fork point serves proofs that hash to the canonical state root there (window and views read in one MDBX read transaction, so a concurrent save cannot prune a height from under the check); every valid delivery is taken (a `ParentHashMismatch` is accepted only where the model says the engine's tip at that height is another block, which a stale notification can cause); a reorg or revert at or below the window's earliest block is refused with `UnwindBeyondEarliest` naming an earliest block the window held around the call, and ends the case since reth moved on without the store; a reorg whose first block does not build on the stored fork block is refused with the stored hash; at the end of a case, after settling, fewer blocks than the persistence threshold stay buffered. Every engine call runs on its own thread with a 30 s bound, so a stalled or panicked engine fails the case instead of hanging it (#23392).
- **Shrinking**: proptest shrinks the action sequence and the configuration; actions are interpreted against the current state (depths clamp to what reth holds in memory), so every sequence is valid. A failure prints the minimal sequence plus the harness transcript of each step (engine tip, store window, reth head), and the first failing case is printed as found, before shrinking, so a run that nextest cuts short still shows it. A tip the model allows on no path fails at once instead of waiting out the settle bound. `ENGINE_MODEL_TRANSCRIPT=1` prints the transcript of passing cases too.
- **Model unit tests** (`model.rs`, `rstest`): the delivery rules (at or below the tip, next block, parent state missing, beyond the next block, mid-sync, refusals on a stale tip), reorg and revert skip-or-unwind, settling, and the restart bounds.

## Matrix

Sampled per case: reth persistence threshold {7, 50} x state masking {0; 30 only with threshold 50, since reth rejects masking + buffer target >= threshold} x memory-block-buffer target {5} x engine (persistence, backpressure) thresholds {(1, 2), (5, 10)} x proofs path by verification interval {0 (index), 1 (execute), 4 (mixed)} x proof window {1000 (never pruned), 4 (pruned on every save)}. Store: `MdbxProofsStorage` in a tempdir. Masking is a parameter of the persistence model only: on develop reth has no partial persistence, so it only decides which persisted blocks stay in memory (see #23441).

Default 24 cases, up to 24 steps each; `PROPTEST_CASES=<n>` raises it (the config goes through `contextualize_config`, so the other `PROPTEST_*` variables apply too). `rust/.config/nextest.toml` gives the `engine_model` binary a 1 m slow period and a 5 m limit, since the whole proptest is one test and a failing case shrinks for up to a minute on top of the run.

## Seams

- `EngineHandle::tip()` under `cfg(any(test, feature = "test-utils"))`, next to `flush()`: the model has to wait for the sync loop to settle without side effects, and the only other way to read the tip (probing with a block above it) raises the sync target when the engine is behind.
- `tests/live/chain.rs`: the chain and store helpers of `tests/live.rs`, moved so that both integration targets share them (`tests/live.rs` keeps its scenario runner and tests).
- `SimulatedReth::{persisted, revert_to, crash_and_restart}`, and `reorg_block`, `reorg_block_without_data` and `UNRELATED_PARENT` moved there from `reorg_revert_edges.rs` so both targets share them; `BlockView::read_from(provider, ...)` and `ProofTarget::accounts(...)`.

Left for later, from the `rust-code-reviewer` pass: a shared `DiskSnapshot` in `store_view.rs` (`reorg_revert_edges.rs` has one), one store wrapper with hooks instead of `StoreWithSaveFaults`, `StoreWithWriteGate` and `StoreWithReadHook`, and `Scenario::assert_tip` reading `engine.tip()` instead of probing.

## Local verification

```
cd rust
cargo test -p reth-optimism-trie --test engine_model
# test result: ok. 17 passed; 0 failed; 3 ignored; finished in 14.01s  (the proptest at 24 cases plus the model's unit cases)

PROPTEST_CASES=120 cargo test -p reth-optimism-trie --test engine_model
# test result: ok. 17 passed; 0 failed; 3 ignored; finished in 62.54s
# (an earlier 200-case run before the review pass: 99.01s)

cargo nextest run -p reth-optimism-trie --test engine_model
# Summary [  21.027s] 17 tests run: 17 passed, 3 skipped

cargo test -p reth-optimism-trie --test live
# test result: ok. 129 passed; 0 failed; 16 ignored; finished in 53.75s

cargo test -p reth-optimism-trie
# unittests 249 passed in 25.78s; engine_model 12.92s; tests/lib 0.16s; live 54.89s; doctests 0.26s: about 94 s in all (run before the review pass)

cargo clippy -p reth-optimism-trie --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings   # clean
cargo +nightly-2026-08-22 fmt --all -- --check                                   # clean
```

## Tracked bugs reproduced (ignored, naming the issue)

**ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#464** (store ahead of reth after an unclean shutdown). `engine_and_store_follow_the_model_through_crashes_rebuilding_a_different_chain` is the random run with `Crash(Different)` enabled; it shrinks to the two-step sequence that `store_follows_reth_through_a_crash_rebuilding_a_different_chain` replays deterministically:

```
minimal failing input: config = Config { cadence: (persistence 1, backpressure 2), persistence: threshold 7, verification_interval: 0, window: 1000 },
actions = [Commit { count: 1 }, Crash(Different)]

Error: the store's latest block 1:0x1e41e789dfc0bb9a57adb1b27b9a31fce50bb89feacc13f39c0f3295ee19f307 is not on the canonical chain, whose block 1 is 0x4f527f04ca93da271b1fd73d0e552863b36888b1b9852b5ab312ad8f72a2a20b
--- steps ---
step 0: Commit { count: 1 }
  engine tip 1, store blocks 0..=0, reth head 1
step 1: Crash(Different)
  crash: reth loses blocks 1..=1 and rebuilds them (Different)
  restart: the store serves through block 1, reth's head is 0
```

The harness restarts the ExEx the way it starts today (fresh engine, `sync_to(best)`, live notifications). #23358 adds a startup reconcile to the ExEx; the PR that un-skips these cases has to add the same step to `Harness::crash`.

**ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#478** (`FinishedHeight` acknowledges heights not yet persisted). `sync_loop_completes_while_reth_prunes_bodies_through_the_acknowledged_tip` runs `[SyncTo { count: 40 }, Commit { count: 1 }]` with reth pruning bodies through the acknowledged tip (`Config::body_pruning`):

```
Error: the engine did not settle within 30s: its tip is NumHash { number: 0, hash: 0x37f157e831e926dc33d479b5c3a6fabefdeeffd9e1735075959b45878a66602b }, the model expects one of [NumHash { number: 40, hash: 0x178862dcc49ec13002cb60187c4a81b188b0cd36ac274a5a943cd02323b04ecc }], the store holds blocks 0..=0
--- steps ---
step 0: SyncTo { count: 40 }
  reth pruned bodies through block 32
```

The pruner model is `SimulatedReth::prune_bodies_through` from #23449, called with the notification tip the ExEx acknowledges.

## Findings from the random runs

- The first runs failed on a harness race, not an engine bug: reading the window and the block views in separate read transactions let a save that pruned the window land in between. `BlockView::read_from` reads them from one transaction now.
- A stale `ChainCommitted` whose parent the sync loop has already replaced makes the engine return `ParentHashMismatch` (its tip at that height is the replacing block). That is the engine's contract and the model predicts it; for the ExEx it is fatal (`handle_notification` returns the error). The window is narrow (the loop has to cross the reorg point while the ExEx processes the stale notification) and no issue tracks it yet; it is not reproduced deterministically here.

Stacked on #23449, #23445, #23442, #23441, #23437, #23434, #23429, #23428, #23421 and #23418.

Closes #23381

topPRs.title: op-reth: test the proofs engine reorg and revert edges and check unwind targets
topPRs.author: einar-oplabs
topPRs.body:
Deterministic tests for the proofs engine's reorg, revert and unwind tasks at the boundaries the model-based test may not reach, with the two engine checks they found missing, and the ExEx executing a reorged chain that carries no trie data instead of failing the node.

The reorg task never checked the first new block's parent against the stored fork block, and nothing refused an unwind at or below the window's earliest block before the store saw it (MDBX refuses it; the in-memory store underflowed at block 0 and otherwise removed the earliest block). `handle_chain_reorged` returned an error for a new chain without trie data, which reth turns into a node exit.

## Changes

- `EngineState::unwind` (shared by the reorg and unwind tasks) now drains any in-flight save, then before touching anything refuses a target at or below `earliest` (`EngineError::Storage(UnwindBeyondEarliest)`) and a target whose parent differs from the stored block below it (`ParentHashMismatch`). The stores keep only the window's end hashes, so the engine buffer retains the hashes of the blocks it persisted (bounded to 1024) to verify forks below the disk tip within a process lifetime. A restarted engine cannot verify a fork below its disk tip; that cell is an `#[ignore]`d test (see below).
- `EngineHandle::reorg` takes `Vec<ReorgBlock>`, each block either `Index { block, hashed_state, trie_updates }` or `Execute(block)`; the task runs each through the same code as `index_block` and `execute_block`, so every block gets the gap and parent checks (an executed block the engine has to skip no longer lets the next indexed one land on a gap). The ExEx picks per block with the rule `ChainCommitted` uses (trie data present and verification not due → index, else execute), shared in `precomputed_trie_data`.
- `PersistenceState::unwind` no longer waits for the in-flight save itself; `EngineState::unwind` drains it first, in one place. The two rejections log at `warn`.
- `InMemoryProofsStorage::unwind_history` follows the trait contract: no-op above `latest`, `UnwindBeyondEarliest` at or below `earliest`, no underflow.
- `ParentHashMismatch`'s docs now describe the unwind case too.

## Tests

Engine live tests in `rust/op-reth/crates/trie/tests/live/reorg_revert_edges.rs`, over backend {InMemory, Mdbx} × flush cadence {(1, 2), (5, 10)} unless noted, each on a seven-block transfer chain. The engine's tip is read through the parent check of a probe block; the persisted history is compared table by table with a fresh store indexed over reth's final canonical chain (`BlockView` / `assert_same_view`), and its proofs are verified against reth's state roots.

| Case | Test | Cells |
|---|---|---|
| baseline | `reorg_replaces_the_stored_blocks_above_the_fork` | × path {Index at fork 6, Execute at fork 3, Mixed at fork 4} |
| (a) | `reorg_not_building_on_the_stored_fork_block_fails_and_changes_nothing` | × fork {6 (buffer or save), 2 (save), 0 (anchor)} × path |
| (a) restart | `restarted_engine_rejects_a_reorg_not_building_on_a_block_below_its_disk_tip` | `#[ignore]`, see Findings |
| (b) | `unwind_or_reorg_at_or_below_the_earliest_block_fails_and_changes_nothing` | × {unwind at earliest, reorg below earliest, reorg at the anchor below a pruned window, unwind at the anchor as earliest} |
| (b) control | `unwind_to_the_block_above_the_earliest_keeps_only_the_earliest` | pruned window |
| (b) in flight | `unwind_at_a_block_the_in_flight_save_prunes_fails_after_the_save` | pruned window; pins that the checks run against the window as the in-flight save leaves it |
| (c) | `revert_of_buffered_blocks_unwinds_the_buffer_and_leaves_the_disk_untouched` | cadence (5, 10) only × revert from {6, 7} |
| (c) in flight | `revert_sent_during_an_in_flight_save_ends_with_the_disk_as_it_was` | |
| (d) | `reorg_sent_during_an_in_flight_save_ends_consistent_with_reth` | × path |

A `StoreWithWriteGate` holds the engine's next write transaction so the save stays in flight until the case releases it. Whether the engine dequeues the revert or reorg before or after the held save completes is not observable from outside (both orders must end the same, and the tests assert that end state); the pruned-window in-flight case is the one where the order changes the outcome, and it pins it. `SimulatedReth` gained `reorg_with(number, specs)`, `executed_block`, `genesis`, `num_hash` and `spawn_engine_with_window`; `FlushCadence` and `Backend` moved to `live.rs` for sharing.

Under cadence (1, 2) no block stays in the buffer outside a save in flight, so (c)'s "(1, 2)" cells are the in-flight revert test.

ExEx tests in `rust/op-reth/crates/exex/src/lib.rs`:
- (e) `chain_reorged_without_trie_data_executes_the_new_chain` × backend: reth's canonical in-memory state holds the new chain, the notification carries no trie data, the store ends on the new tip and `FinishedHeight` acknowledges it.
- (f) `chain_reorged_with_different_fork_blocks_fails_and_changes_nothing`: the error is returned, the store keeps its tip, no event is sent. `handle_chain_reorged`'s docs state the expectation.
- `precomputed_trie_data_follows_the_verification_interval`: a table over interval {0, 2} × block × trie data present/absent.

Unit tests: `engine::buffer::state` (`hash_at` through prune and unwind, bound), `engine::state` (unwind at the anchor, unwind onto a contradicted parent), and `tests/lib.rs` `test_unwind_history_*` over both backends.

## Local verification

All from `rust/` with the shared target dir, on the final commit:

- `cargo test -p reth-optimism-trie --test live` — 120 passed, 8 ignored (6 pre-existing `abandoned_fork` cells from #23441 and the 2 restart cells here), 40.0 s wall for the whole live target (21.9 s before this PR).
- `cargo test -p reth-optimism-trie --test live -- reorg_revert_edges` — 64 passed, 2 ignored, 18.3 s.
- `cargo test -p reth-optimism-trie --lib` — 248 passed (28 under `engine::`, including the 5 new buffer and state tests).
- `cargo test -p reth-optimism-trie --test lib` — 94 passed (8 of them the new `test_unwind_history_*` cells over InMemory and Mdbx).
- `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test -p reth-optimism-exex --lib` — 19 passed (12 existing, 2 new reorg tests, 5 `precomputed_trie_data` cases); `cargo test -p reth-optimism-exex --doc --all-features` — 1 passed (the crate doctest needs `--all-features` for `OP_MAINNET`, as `just test-docs` runs it; unchanged by this PR).
- `cargo clippy -p reth-optimism-trie -p reth-optimism-exex --all-targets` — zero warnings; `just fmt-check` — clean.

The `rust-code-reviewer` agent ran on the diff; its findings (the reorg task's `Index` arm bypassing `index_block`'s checks, the drain-before-check ordering untested, the in-flight test names, dead code in `PersistenceState::unwind`, naming and dedup) are addressed above.

Every matrix cell of the engine tests ran locally (both backends × both cadences); the only cells not run are the `#[ignore]`d restart cells, which fail by design today.

## Findings

- (a) and (b) fail on develop without the engine checks: with `self.check_unwind_target(to)?` removed from `EngineState::unwind`, all 28 cells of the two tests fail. (a) `reorg_not_building_on_the_stored_fork_block_fails_and_changes_nothing`: all 12 cells panic with `the reorg does not build on the stored fork block: ()`, i.e. `EngineHandle::reorg` returned `Ok(())` and inserted the chain on the wrong parent. (b) `unwind_or_reorg_at_or_below_the_earliest_block_fails_and_changes_nothing`: the 8 Mdbx cells get `got Persistence(Storage(UnwindBeyondEarliest { .. }))`, the store refusing only after the engine drained the save and sent the unwind to the persistence service; with develop's `InMemoryProofsStorage::unwind_history` the 8 InMemory cells panic with `the unwind would remove the window's earliest block: ()`, the unwind returning `Ok(())` after removing the earliest block.
- A restarted engine knows no hash below its store's latest block, so a reorg onto a wrong fork block there is accepted; `restarted_engine_rejects_a_reorg_not_building_on_a_block_below_its_disk_tip` is `#[ignore]`d naming this issue and #23385. Fixing it means keeping every block's hash in the store (a schema change), which is out of this issue's scope.
- The in-memory store's `unwind_history` subtracted one from the target without checking `earliest` or `latest`, so an unwind to block 0 panicked the persistence thread and an unwind above `latest` moved `latest` to a block it never stored.

topPRs.title: op-acceptance-tests,op-devstack: cover eth version negotiation and transaction propagation between op-reth and op-geth
topPRs.author: einar-oplabs
topPRs.body:
Nothing checked how op-reth and op-geth peer and exchange transactions: `rust/op-reth/crates/node/tests/it/p2p_version.rs` pins the version two op-reth nodes negotiate, and every devstack peering is trusted, which exempts the session from the reputation handling the reth 2.6 bump (#23046) changes along with the default protocol (eth/71) and the transaction fetcher (reth#26924, a per-peer cap of 4096 announced hashes). This adds an acceptance test package that peers an op-reth follower and an op-geth follower as basic peers and checks the negotiated version, transaction propagation in both directions, and op-reth under an announcement burst from op-geth, written against hooks that are the same on `develop` and on the bump.

## What the tests cover

All three tests run on a `pairSystem` (`op-acceptance-tests/tests/op_reth_opgeth_peering/system_test.go`): an op-reth sequencer, an op-reth follower and an op-geth follower, 1s blocks. One follower is the *sender*: it is kept off the mixed runtime's trusted mesh (`IsolateFromL2P2P`), its consensus client is peered with the sequencer's alone, and it dials the other follower (the *receiver*) with the new `PeerWithBasic`, so the receiver is its only execution-layer peer and the session is trusted on neither side. The receiver keeps the trusted peering with the sequencer that the runtime set up. A transaction submitted to the sender can therefore only reach the sequencer through the receiver, so its inclusion proves it crossed the peering under test; with the sequencer paused, the receiver's pool can be observed. The system is returned once the sender has filled its gap to the chain through the receiver.

- `TestOpRethAndOpGethNegotiateTheHighestCommonEthVersion`, subtests `op-reth_dials_op-geth` and `op-geth_dials_op-reth`: both sides must report the same negotiated eth version through `admin_peers`, equal to the highest version both advertise (`sysgo.HighestCommonEthVersion` over the two `caps` lists), and the advertised versions are logged.
- `TestTransactionCrossesTheOpRethOpGethPeeringIntoABlock`, subtests `op-reth_to_op-geth` and `op-geth_to_op-reth`: with the sequencer paused, a transfer submitted to the sender must show up in the receiver's pool (`eth_getTransactionByHash` with no block), and once the sequencer resumes both followers must see it in the same block.
- `TestOpRethKeepsItsOpGethPeerThroughAnAnnouncementBurst`: op-geth is the sender. 4112 fresh accounts (the cap plus one fan-out of 16) each submit one transaction with 4096 bytes of zero calldata to op-geth in batch calls while the sequencer is paused. op-geth sends a transaction larger than its `txMaxBroadcastSize` (4096 bytes) to no peer whole: it announces the hash (`eth/handler.go`, `BroadcastTransactions`), so the burst is 4112 `NewPooledTransactionHashes` entries to op-reth within about a second, which op-reth has to fetch. The test requires op-reth's pool to reach at least 4096 of them, op-reth to keep the same session with op-geth (same remote port in `admin_peers`; a drop followed by op-geth's static re-dial would show a new one) and to log nothing at error level, and once the sequencer resumes, op-reth's pool to drain down to at most 16 and its head to keep advancing. How many of the burst op-reth fetched and how many each follower still holds afterwards are logged.

What the burst can and cannot show: the number of hashes announced exceeds what op-reth tracks per peer after the bump, but op-reth fetches while the burst is still arriving, and whether its unfetched set from op-geth ever reached 4096 (the point where it drops further announcements) is not observable through RPC. The test therefore proves that op-reth takes a cap-sized announcement burst from an untrusted op-geth peer in its stride, not that the drop path ran. Proving the latter needs reth's `announced_hashes_dropped_peer_limit` metric, which the mixed runtime does not expose. The drain bound of 16 rather than 0 is for the same cap downstream: op-reth passes the burst to the sequencer, which fetches what op-reth only announced to it, so a cap-sized fetch there can strand up to one fan-out in op-reth's pool; every run below drained to 0.

Each sender has exactly one transaction, so a hash the fetcher drops cannot leave a nonce gap behind; the accounts are funded through a tree of distributors (`funding_test.go`) because reth holds at most 16 transactions per account (`--txpool.max-account-slots`, and the runtime passes `--txpool.nolocals`), which also bounds every funding round to one batch per payer.

Matrix: direction {op-reth to op-geth, op-geth to op-reth} as subtests (the dialing side is the sender, so both dial directions are covered too); CL {op-node, kona-node} through `DEVSTACK_L2CL_KIND`. Skips on `DEVSTACK_L2EL_KIND=op-geth` (the sequencer is this tree's op-reth).

## Local verification

Debug op-reth built from this stack's Rust tree (identical to `develop`'s), kona-node release binary from `develop`'s `rust/kona`, `-parallel 2`, under `caffeinate`:

```
cd <worktree> && DEVSTACK_ORCHESTRATOR=sysgo RUST_BINARY_PATH_OP_RETH=<op-reth> RUST_BINARY_PATH_KONA_NODE=<kona-node> \
  go test -count=1 -timeout 40m -parallel 2 -run 'TestOpRethAndOpGethNegotiateTheHighestCommonEthVersion|TestTransactionCrossesTheOpRethOpGethPeeringIntoABlock|TestOpRethKeepsItsOpGethPeerThroughAnAnnouncementBurst' -v ./op-acceptance-tests/tests/op_reth_opgeth_peering/
```

`develop` op-reth, op-node (default): all five cells pass, 69s for the package.

```
--- PASS: TestOpRethKeepsItsOpGethPeerThroughAnAnnouncementBurst (37.56s)
--- PASS: TestTransactionCrossesTheOpRethOpGethPeeringIntoABlock/op-reth_to_op-geth (23.08s)
--- PASS: TestTransactionCrossesTheOpRethOpGethPeeringIntoABlock/op-geth_to_op-reth (23.02s)
--- PASS: TestOpRethAndOpGethNegotiateTheHighestCommonEthVersion/op-reth_dials_op-geth (20.54s)
--- PASS: TestOpRethAndOpGethNegotiateTheHighestCommonEthVersion/op-geth_dials_op-reth (21.94s)
```

`develop` op-reth, `DEVSTACK_L2CL_KIND=kona-node`: all five cells pass, 100s.

```
--- PASS: TestOpRethKeepsItsOpGethPeerThroughAnAnnouncementBurst (46.95s)
--- PASS: TestTransactionCrossesTheOpRethOpGethPeeringIntoABlock/op-reth_to_op-geth (36.33s)
--- PASS: TestTransactionCrossesTheOpRethOpGethPeeringIntoABlock/op-geth_to_op-reth (33.36s)
--- PASS: TestOpRethAndOpGethNegotiateTheHighestCommonEthVersion/op-reth_dials_op-geth (31.98s)
--- PASS: TestOpRethAndOpGethNegotiateTheHighestCommonEthVersion/op-geth_dials_op-reth (29.74s)
```

Against #23046's op-reth (reth 2.6.0, built from the bump head 93d9ec9d2f, op-node): all five cells pass, 71s.

```
--- PASS: TestOpRethKeepsItsOpGethPeerThroughAnAnnouncementBurst (36.82s)
--- PASS: TestTransactionCrossesTheOpRethOpGethPeeringIntoABlock/op-reth_to_op-geth (22.28s)
--- PASS: TestTransactionCrossesTheOpRethOpGethPeeringIntoABlock/op-geth_to_op-reth (28.46s)
--- PASS: TestOpRethAndOpGethNegotiateTheHighestCommonEthVersion/op-reth_dials_op-geth (23.69s)
--- PASS: TestOpRethAndOpGethNegotiateTheHighestCommonEthVersion/op-geth_dials_op-reth (19.67s)
```

Negotiated versions, as the verification criterion asks: op-geth v1.101702.4-rc.1 advertises `eth/69` only (`eth/protocols/eth/protocol.go`, `ProtocolVersions = {ETH69}`). `develop`'s op-reth advertises `eth/66` to `eth/69`, the bump's `eth/66` to `eth/71`; the pair negotiates **eth/69** on both, in both dial directions, so on the bump op-reth falls back two versions from its own eth/71 to op-geth's highest. The peering is untrusted on both sides (asserted inside `PeerWithBasic`); op-reth marks op-geth's entry static when op-reth dials, op-geth marks op-reth's static when op-geth dials.

Burst: op-reth's pool held 4107 to 4112 of the 4112 at the first poll after the batches were accepted, on `develop` and on the bump alike (4105 to 4112 across all runs), the session kept its remote port and eth/69, no op-reth error log, and after the sequencer resumed every burst transaction was included within 6s: 0 left in op-reth and 0 left in op-geth in every run.

Unit: `go test ./op-service/txplan/ ./op-devstack/sysgo/ -run 'TestHighest|TestPeerInfo|TestPeerIDMatches|TestPollPeerList|TestPinnedFields'` and `go test -run TestFunding ./op-acceptance-tests/tests/op_reth_opgeth_peering/` pass; `linter/bin/op-golangci-lint run` on the changed packages reports no issue.

## Observations

- An isolated op-geth follower under op-node logs `Failed to get payload ... err="Unsupported fork"` while it is behind the chain: op-node derives attributes from L1 and asks op-geth to seal them, which op-geth refuses under the devnet's Karst-at-genesis config. The follower catches up through the receiver instead, and the same lines appear on `develop`; noted, not investigated.
- On this machine, under two concurrent devnets, an op-geth follower that is both gap-filling and peered with two consensus clients once answered its user RPC with `dial tcp 127.0.0.1:<port>: i/o timeout` for 30s. The pair keeps the sender's consensus client on a single peer (the sequencer's), which never showed it in nine runs since.

## Seams

- `sysgo.ConnectP2PBasic` / `dsl.L2ELNode.PeerWithBasic`: a basic peering (static entry on the dialer, nothing on the acceptor, trusted on neither side, asserted after connecting). `PeerWith` stays trusted on both sides; `DisconnectPeerWith` undoes `PeerWith` only.
- `dsl.L2ELNode.VerifyPeeredWith`, `PeerInfoOf`, `Peers` over `sysgo.PeerInfo` / `ListPeers` / `ELPeerInfo` (caps, negotiated eth version or 0 during the handshake, inbound/static/trusted, session addresses), `sysgo.HighestEthVersion` and `HighestCommonEthVersion`.
- `dsl.L2ELNode.SendTransactions` (batched `eth_sendRawTransaction`), `WaitForPooledTransaction`, `TxPoolStatus`, `TxPoolReached`, `TxPoolHoldsAtMost`, `TxPoolDrained`.
- `dsl.EOA.PlanOffline`, `Sign`, `Submit`; `txplan.WithStaticChainID`. `txplan.WithGasFeeCap` now drops the default fee-cap computation the way `WithGasLimit` drops the estimator, so a pinned fee cap stays pinned when the tip cap is pinned after it or a block is fetched (it was silently recomputed from the tip cap and the base fee); the one existing caller, `op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/loadtest/l2.go`, now gets the 10,000 gwei cap it asked for, which its budget already accounts for.

`go-code-reviewer` was run and every finding addressed: the `bigint` lint, the burst's claim re-scoped as above and its drain bound, both followers gated on the funding blocks before the burst and the transfer, the expected version as the highest common one rather than the smaller maximum, `Peers` listing handshaking peers too, the session check guarded to the accepting side, per-poll logging in the pool waits, and the setup re-checks, unused `Fn` variant, duplicated node-info lookups and inaccurate comments removed.

Stacked on #23440, #23438, #23436, #23431, #23427, #23421 and #23418.

Closes #23402

topPRs.title: op-acceptance-tests,op-devstack,op-reth: hold the sequencer to its block schedule across persistence runs
topPRs.author: einar-oplabs
topPRs.body:
Nothing held an op-reth sequencer to its block schedule across reth's persistence runs: the fork fix reth#26708 existed because persistence stalled payload building, and the reth 2.6 bump (#23046) replaces that mechanism with upstream's overlay snapshots, makes persistence batches about seven times larger (threshold 7 to 50) and deletes the fork's regression test `rust/op-reth/crates/node/tests/it/payload_handoff.rs`. This adds an acceptance test that keeps a sequencer under load for at least three persistence runs and fails on the first missed slot, and a node-level test that stalls a persistence batch inside the database and requires the next payload job to finish within the block time, written against hooks that survive the bump.

## What the tests cover

### `op-acceptance-tests/tests/op_reth_sequencer_persistence`

`TestOpRethSequencerKeepsScheduleAcrossPersistenceRuns`: an op-reth sequencer alone (no proofs history, so reth's persistence is the only one on it) on `--engine.persistence-threshold={7,50}` with `--engine.memory-block-buffer-target=5` and 1s blocks, with the batcher the mixed runtime attaches. A package-local workload keeps it under load from two accounts off the test goroutine, in rounds of 8 transactions submitted back to back with the last one awaited: either transfers between the accounts, or calls to a contract that creates 16 storage slots it has never written per call (`dsl.EOA.DeployStorageFiller`), so every persistence run writes a batch of new state. The test holds the sequencer to its schedule for three times the threshold in blocks through the new `dsl.L2ELNode.AdvancedOnSchedule` wait, stops the load (failing if it had failed first), and requires op-reth to have logged nothing at error level meanwhile (`RecordLogs` from #23427).

Three times the threshold puts at least three persistence runs inside the window wherever it starts: reth persists once more than the threshold of blocks sit in memory and keeps the last 5, so a run starts every threshold+1-5 blocks (at threshold 50 at blocks 51, 97, 143, ...; at threshold 7 every three blocks).

Matrix: threshold {7, 50} x load {transfers, storage_writes} as subtests, CL {op-node, kona-node} through `DEVSTACK_L2CL_KIND` (CI runs both). Skips on op-geth.

### `dsl.L2ELNode.AdvancedOnSchedule(blocks, blockTime)`

Waits for the unsafe head to be on schedule (a sequencer that starts behind its genesis time builds back-to-back blocks until it has caught up, bounded by `ScheduleOpts.CatchUpTimeout`), then samples the head eight times per block time until it has advanced `blocks` blocks, and fails as soon as a slot is missed: every new block must extend the previous head, carry the previous head's timestamp plus the block time, and be seen canonical before its own timestamp plus the block time has passed on the wall clock, which is when the next block is due; a block not seen within a further block time of being due fails the wait before it arrives. The pure check `blockOnSchedule` has a table test. The wait logs the largest lag it saw.

### `rust/op-reth/crates/node/tests/it/payload_during_persistence.rs`

`payload_job_completes_while_persistence_batch_is_in_flight`, an `rstest` table over threshold {7, 50} (reth 2.5's and 2.6's defaults). It launches the op-reth node on a `WriteGatedDatabase`, a `Database` wrapper injected through `NodeBuilder::with_database` that delegates everything and parks every write transaction at a gate right after opening it while the gate is closed. reth's persistence service opens its write transaction (`database_provider_rw`) before it writes anything in `on_save_blocks`, so closing the gate right before a batch is due keeps that batch in flight inside its transaction with nothing committed, and the test decides when it lands. The scenario, through the engine API like a consensus client (forkchoiceUpdated with attributes, engine_getPayloadV3, engine_newPayloadV3, forkchoiceUpdated):

1. Build `threshold` blocks; nothing is on disk yet.
2. Close the gate and build one more block, which with `memory_block_buffer_target = 0` makes reth persist the whole chain as one batch; wait for the persistence service to be parked.
3. Start a payload job and require it to resolve within 2s (OP Mainnet's block time) with the batch still parked, and the disk still at genesis.
4. Start another payload job with the batch parked, then release the batch while the job runs and wait for it to reach the disk. Send a transfer to the pool, wait for the job's best payload to be rebuilt with it (so the rebuild read state after the batch landed), and require the job to resolve within 2s and its payload to be valid under newPayload, which checks the state root the builder computed across the batch's landing. Then wait for the in-memory state to drop the batch.
5. Build one more block on the persisted base.

A guard opens the gate when dropped, so a failed assertion cannot leave the persistence service parked through shutdown. Every engine call and wait is bounded at 20s with a message naming the stalled step.

The deleted `payload_handoff.rs` tested the fork's mechanism (`suppress_persistence_during_build`, the deferred persisted handoff, the persistence-completion metric), none of which exists after the bump. The replacement uses only `NodeBuilder::with_database`, the `Database` trait, `PayloadBuilderHandle::best_payload` and the in-memory state's persisted marker, all unchanged on the #23046 pin (reth rev 8d359d0), so it is the regression test that carries over. Step 4 is the window the fork protected (a batch landing while a job holds the old overlay) and the one 2.6 changes (the job keeps its own snapshot and persistence reclaims the overlay at once), covered the same way on both.

## Local verification

Run with this tree's debug op-reth (built by the previous agent of the stack from the same Rust tree) and the kona-node release copied out of the shared cargo target, contracts prebuilt:

```
RUST_BINARY_PATH_OP_RETH=<copy of rust/target/debug/op-reth> RUST_BINARY_PATH_KONA_NODE=<copy of rust/target/release/kona-node> \
  go test -count=1 -timeout 30m -parallel 2 -run 'TestOpRethSequencerKeepsScheduleAcrossPersistenceRuns' -v ./op-acceptance-tests/tests/op_reth_sequencer_persistence/
```

op-node (default), all four cells pass, 234s for the package at `-parallel 2` (the run of the final code; an earlier run before the review changes passed with the same shape of numbers):

| cell | blocks held to schedule | rounds included (transactions) | largest lag seen | time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| threshold_7-transfers | 6 to 27 | 17 (136) | 74ms | 34s |
| threshold_7-storage_writes | 7 to 28 | 18 (144) | 77ms | 35s |
| threshold_50-transfers | 6 to 156 | 130 (1040) | 80ms | 163s |
| threshold_50-storage_writes | 7 to 157 | 132 (1056) | 79ms | 164s |

About seven transactions per block; the threshold-50 storage cell created 16,896 storage slots over 150 blocks, about 5,000 per persistence run. No block was later than half a block time (the wait logs those at warning level) and no op-reth error log in any cell. The runs below were made while cargo builds for this PR ran on the same machine.

With `DEVSTACK_L2CL_KIND=kona-node` (kona-node release from this tree's `rust/kona` at the base commit), all four cells pass, 204s for the package (final code; an earlier run before the review changes passed the same way):

| cell | blocks held to schedule | rounds included (transactions) | largest lag seen | time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| threshold_7-transfers | 6 to 27 | 17 (136) | 127ms | 38s |
| threshold_7-storage_writes | 7 to 28 | 15 (120) | 118ms | 35s |
| threshold_50-transfers | 6 to 156 | 124 (992) | 175ms | 167s |
| threshold_50-storage_writes | 7 to 157 | 126 (1008) | 128ms | 164s |

No cell needed the catch-up wait under either CL: the workload's setup covered the blocks the sequencer builds back to back after start.

Against #23046's op-reth (reth 2.6.0, built from the bump head 93d9ec9d2f, op-node CL), all four cells pass, 202s for the package:

| cell | blocks held to schedule | rounds included (transactions) | largest lag seen | time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| threshold_7-transfers | 10 to 31 | 18 (144) | 76ms | 38s |
| threshold_7-storage_writes | 7 to 28 | 16 (128) | 78ms | 35s |
| threshold_50-transfers | 10 to 160 | 129 (1032) | 92ms | 166s |
| threshold_50-storage_writes | 7 to 157 | 130 (1040) | 92ms | 164s |

So the verification criterion holds on both: no missed slot on `develop` and on #23046, under both thresholds and both loads.

Rust (`cd rust && cargo test -p reth-optimism-node --test it payload_during_persistence`):

```
test payload_during_persistence::payload_job_completes_while_persistence_batch_is_in_flight::case_1_reth_2_5_default ... ok
test payload_during_persistence::payload_job_completes_while_persistence_batch_is_in_flight::case_2_reth_2_6_default ... ok
test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 20 filtered out; finished in 2.32s
```

Negative control (not committed): with `config.engine.persistence_backpressure_threshold = Some(persistence_threshold + 1)` the parked batch makes the engine backpressure at the batch tip, and both cases fail as they should with `forkchoice update with attributes stalled` after the 20s call bound, with the gate guard letting the node shut down (43s for both cases, no hang).

`cargo clippy -p reth-optimism-node --all-targets -- -D warnings` and the pinned nightly `just fmt-fix` are clean. (Locally, rustc 1.95 hit an incremental-compilation ICE, "unstable fingerprints for evaluate_obligation", twice while iterating on this test target; `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` sidesteps it and CI builds are not incremental.)

Unit: `go test -run TestBlockOnSchedule ./op-devstack/dsl/` passes.

## Corrections to the issue

- "Assert every block's timestamp delta equals the block time and that no slot is missed": on the OP Stack the timestamp delta alone cannot catch a stall. Both op-node and kona-node always stamp a block with its parent's timestamp plus the block time; a sequencer that stalls falls behind the wall clock and then catches up with back-to-back blocks, and the timestamps never show it. The wait checks the timestamp delta as asked, and anchors "missed slot" to the wall clock: a block is late when it is not canonical before its own timestamp plus the block time, that is before the next block is due.
- "Using the hooks upstream exposes after the handoff removal": upstream exposes no persistence hook. `TempDatabase`'s transaction hooks wrap read transactions only. What both pins expose is `NodeBuilder::with_database` with any `Database` implementation, and the persistence service's write transaction is the first thing a batch takes, so a gated database is the seam. Stated in the test's module comment.

## Seams

- `dsl.L2ELNode.AdvancedOnSchedule` / `AdvancedOnScheduleFn` with `ScheduleOpts`: holds a chain to its block schedule; the first DSL wait on block cadence.
- `dsl.EOA.DeployStorageFiller(slotsPerCall)`: a contract whose every call creates that many storage slots it has never written, for loads that must grow state.
- The workload (two senders, rounds off the test goroutine) is package-local like the crash and upgrade packages' workloads; it is the fourth copy of the shape and the follow-up to fold them into the DSL now has four inputs.

`go-code-reviewer` and `rust-code-reviewer` were both run and every finding addressed: the workload goroutine is now joined in a `t.Cleanup` so a failed schedule wait stops the load before the nodes it drives; every transaction of a round is checked, not just the last; the block time comes from the chain config rather than the test's constant, and the wait rejects a block time that is not whole seconds; the ancestor fetch is bounded and retried; the overdue arithmetic shares one boundary definition with the per-block check and has its own table test; the catch-up wait logs once per head; a block later than half a block time is logged at warning level so a CI failure shows lag climbing before the failing block. On the Rust side the batch is parked inside the real write transaction rather than before it, a timed job now spans the batch landing (the window the fork protected), the gate uses `Condvar::wait_while` and closing it returns the reopen guard, the watchdog thread that could not fire under nextest's 120s timeout and would have killed the sibling case under `cargo test` is gone, and tautological assertions were dropped.

Stacked on #23431, #23427, #23421 and #23418.

Closes #23397
